prs.author: keurcien
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Tokens loaded from storage on restart never get their token_expiry_time populated, so is_token_valid() treats a stale/expired stored token as valid, the proactive-refresh branch in async_auth_flow is skipped, and the client ends up forcing a full interactive re-authorization instead of a silent refresh. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Tokens loaded from storage on restart never get their token_expiry_time populated, so is_token_valid() treats a stale/expired stored token as valid, the proactive-refresh branch in async_auth_flow is skipped, and the client ends up forcing a full interactive re-authorization instead of a silent refresh. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Fixes the defect at its source: _initialize() now calls context.update_token_expiry() when loaded tokens carry expires_in, a 4-line change with a dedicated expired_tokens fixture/test. #2875's own inline comment names this exact same root cause ('a provider reloaded from storage never restores token_expiry_time...') but instead patches around it with a larger addition (a new refresh attempt inside the 401 handler) that only kicks in after a request has already been sent and rejected. Once token_expiry_time is restored correctly, the existing proactive-refresh path already in async_auth_flow handles the expired token before the request goes out, so the request never reaches the 401 branch #2875 modifies for this scenario.

prs.title: Fix substring matches in WWW-Authenticate parsing
prs.author: Whning0513
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same underlying bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: the WWW-Authenticate header parser previously split/matched on raw substrings (e.g. naive comma-splitting or substring checks) which breaks when a quoted auth-param value contains a comma, or which can misidentify challenges via substring matches instead of proper scheme-boundary detection. Both add a quote-aware, escape-aware tokenizer to replace the old regex/substring approach (PR #3012 removes `import re` entirely). (2 PRs)

prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #3041 tokenizes the entire header into top-level comma-separated segments and then determines the scheme for each segment independently via partition-on-space + case-insensitive scheme comparison (`_extract_bearer_auth_params`), which correctly handles headers containing multiple challenges (e.g. `Basic ..., Bearer ...`). PR #3012's `_iter_www_auth_params` instead locates only the first space in the whole header and treats everything after it as one scheme's params, so it cannot distinguish a second scheme's challenge from an additional auth-param and does not address the substring-match failure mode the bug is named after.

(2 PRs)

prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3056 scopes the skip-condition to exactly `str | None` (the case in its own title/bug report), leaving pre-parsing intact for other simple-type unions like `str | int` where JSON pre-parsing is still needed to coerce a numeric string into an int. #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` instead treats *any* union whose members are all in {str, int, float, bool, NoneType} as skip-parsing, which also disables pre-parsing for `str | int`, `str | float`, and `str | bool` params — a broader behavior change beyond the reported str|None corruption bug. #3056 additionally adds `_unwrap_annotated()` so the check still fires correctly for the common `Annotated[str | None, Field(...)]` signature pattern; #2032's frozenset-membership check does not unwrap Annotated-wrapped union members.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs touch the exact same branch (attempt >= MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS in _handle_reconnection) but resolve it differently. #2395 sends a JSONRPCError through read_stream_writer correlated to the specific pending request via ctx.session_message.message.id, guarded by an isinstance(JSONRPCRequest) check, so only the affected request fails while the rest of the session keeps running. #3098 instead raises a StreamableHTTPError from the reconnection path and adds a new recursive _unwrap_exception() helper solely to pull that error back out of anyio's TaskGroup ExceptionGroup wrapping, propagating the failure as a hard exception through the whole task group rather than resolving just the one request. #2395's fix operates at the same per-request granularity as the bug it fixes and needs no extra exception-unwrapping machinery, so it's the one to keep; #3098's approach and its _unwrap_exception helper become unnecessary once #2395 lands.

clusters.pick_reason: PR #3041 tokenizes the entire header into top-level comma-separated segments and then determines the scheme for each segment independently via partition-on-space + case-insensitive scheme comparison (`_extract_bearer_auth_params`), which correctly handles headers containing multiple challenges (e.g. `Basic ..., Bearer ...`). PR #3012's `_iter_www_auth_params` instead locates only the first space in the whole header and treats everything after it as one scheme's params, so it cannot distinguish a second scheme's challenge from an additional auth-param and does not address the substring-match failure mode the bug is named after.

clusters.pick_reason: Fixes the reported blocking behavior by default with no caller-side configuration required, and includes a regression test (BlockingStdout) that reproduces the stall during progress notifications. #2215's new read/write buffer-size parameters default to 0, so it preserves the exact blocking behavior for every existing caller (including internal stdio_server() usage) unless they opt in — it doesn't resolve the underlying symptom without extra action from downstream code.

members.title: fix(stdio): allow configurable memory stream buffer size

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs touch the exact same branch (attempt >= MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS in _handle_reconnection) but resolve it differently. #2395 sends a JSONRPCError through read_stream_writer correlated to the specific pending request via ctx.session_message.message.id, guarded by an isinstance(JSONRPCRequest) check, so only the affected request fails while the rest of the session keeps running. #3098 instead raises a StreamableHTTPError from the reconnection path and adds a new recursive _unwrap_exception() helper solely to pull that error back out of anyio's TaskGroup ExceptionGroup wrapping, propagating the failure as a hard exception through the whole task group rather than resolving just the one request. #2395's fix operates at the same per-request granularity as the bug it fixes and needs no extra exception-unwrapping machinery, so it's the one to keep; #3098's approach and its _unwrap_exception helper become unnecessary once #2395 lands.

clusters.pick_reason: PR #3041 tokenizes the entire header into top-level comma-separated segments and then determines the scheme for each segment independently via partition-on-space + case-insensitive scheme comparison (`_extract_bearer_auth_params`), which correctly handles headers containing multiple challenges (e.g. `Basic ..., Bearer ...`). PR #3012's `_iter_www_auth_params` instead locates only the first space in the whole header and treats everything after it as one scheme's params, so it cannot distinguish a second scheme's challenge from an additional auth-param and does not address the substring-match failure mode the bug is named after.

members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3041: Both PRs fix the same underlying bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: the WWW-Authenticate header parser previously split/matched on raw substrings (e.g. naive comma-splitting or substring checks) which breaks when a quoted auth-param value contains a comma, or which can misidentify challenges via substring matches instead of proper scheme-boundary detection.
